score.label: Score
score.note: the round's own: seven criteria, 1-5 each

rows.name: Exploded black box
rows.rationale: A box with its lid lifted on dashed guide lines: the part is a black box you can still look into (specs, CAD, sim, prices).

rows.name: Exploded black box
rows.rationale: A box with its lid lifted on dashed guide lines: the part is a black box you can still look into (specs, CAD, sim, prices).

rows.name: Isometric cube with a port
rows.rationale: One solid isometric block with a single connector port cut into its face; the catalog's unit of thought is the part-as-box.

rows.name: Isometric cube with a port
rows.rationale: One solid isometric block with a single connector port cut into its face; the catalog's unit of thought is the part-as-box.

rows.name: Gear inside a box
rows.rationale: A gear sealed inside a square outline: mechanism visible, packaging opaque. The literal reading of 'black box'.

rows.name: Gear inside a box
rows.rationale: A gear sealed inside a square outline: mechanism visible, packaging opaque. The literal reading of 'black box'.

rows.name: Servo horn
rows.rationale: Top view of a four-spoke servo horn with screw holes and shaft screw; instantly readable to anyone who has built an arm.

rows.name: Servo horn
rows.rationale: Top view of a four-spoke servo horn with screw holes and shaft screw; instantly readable to anyone who has built an arm.

rows.name: Part-number tag
rows.rationale: An inventory tag with its string hole, stamped rp in mono: every part in the catalog is a tagged item with a number.

rows.name: Part-number tag

rows.name: L-bracket with slots

rows.name: L-bracket with slots

rows.name: Motor flange face
rows.rationale: NEMA-style chamfered flange, four mounting holes, pilot ring and a shaft: the most recognisable face of an actuator.

rows.name: Motor flange face

rows.name: D-sub connector
rows.rationale: A D-sub connector face with pin 1 marked in the accent: the pinout every datasheet has, drawn as the part itself.

rows.name: D-sub connector

rows.name: Datasheet with tab

rows.name: Datasheet with tab

rows.name: Stack of parts
rows.rationale: Three silhouettes (power supply, driver, actuator) stacked: the catalog's categories as one tower.

rows.name: Stack of parts
rows.rationale: Three silhouettes (power supply, driver, actuator) stacked: the catalog's categories as one tower.

rows.name: parts in a black box
rows.rationale: Pure wordmark: 'robot' plain, 'parts' knocked out of a solid box. The black-box idea is in the type itself.

rows.name: parts in a black box
rows.rationale: Pure wordmark: 'robot' plain, 'parts' knocked out of a solid box. The black-box idea is in the type itself.

rows.name: Dimension line
rows.rationale: Pure wordmark under a drawing dimension line with arrowheads and extension lines; the mark is a dimensioned box.

rows.name: Dimension line

rows.name: Stroke monogram rp
rows.rationale: r and p built from one stroke weight on a shared x-height, p's bowl a true circle. Works alone as a favicon.

rows.name: Stroke monogram rp
rows.rationale: r and p built from one stroke weight on a shared x-height, p's bowl a true circle. Works alone as a favicon.

rows.name: Dot-matrix wordmark
rows.rationale: Pure wordmark in a 5x7 dot grid, 'parts' in the accent: the bolt pattern and the status-LED panel in one texture.

rows.name: Dot-matrix wordmark

rows.name: Drawing title block
rows.rationale: A drawing's title block with rp in the name cell and a revision flag. Capitals in mono, like drawing lettering.

rows.name: Drawing title block
rows.rationale: A drawing's title block with rp in the name cell and a revision flag. Capitals in mono, like drawing lettering.

rows.name: Centre-of-gravity o's
rows.rationale: Both o's become the centre-of-mass target symbol, so the wordmark is monospace with two engineering glyphs in it.

rows.name: Centre-of-gravity o's
rows.rationale: Both o's become the centre-of-mass target symbol, so the wordmark is monospace with two engineering glyphs in it.

rows.name: Inputs and outputs
rows.rationale: The block-diagram black box: two inputs in, one output out. It says 'parts defined by their interface'.

rows.name: Inputs and outputs
rows.rationale: The block-diagram black box: two inputs in, one output out. It says 'parts defined by their interface'.

rows.name: Data-Matrix code
rows.rationale: An 8x8 Data-Matrix label with its solid L and accent clock track: the code etched on real parts.

rows.name: Data-Matrix code

rows.name: Hex nut
rows.rationale: Top view of a hex nut with a chamfer ring and a thread arc. Hardware-store plainness, strong silhouette at 16 px.

rows.name: Hex nut
rows.rationale: Top view of a hex nut with a chamfer ring and a thread arc. Hardware-store plainness, strong silhouette at 16 px.

rows.name: Section view
rows.rationale: An actuator cut in half: 45-degree section hatching around the housing, the rotor in the accent colour.

rows.name: Section view
rows.rationale: An actuator cut in half: 45-degree section hatching around the housing, the rotor in the accent colour.

rows.name: Voxel cube
rows.rationale: R1-02's block rebuilt from a 3x3x3 grid of voxels: the part is itself made of parts. The front corner voxel is the accent, the one module you are looking at.

rows.name: Voxel cube
rows.rationale: R1-02's block rebuilt from a 3x3x3 grid of voxels: the part is itself made of parts. The front corner voxel is the accent, the one module you are looking at.

rows.name: Pixel cube
rows.rationale: R1-02 redrawn as 2:1 pixel art on the 16-cell grid, the way BAM's hammer is drawn in pixels: three shaded faces and a 2x3 copper port. Wordmark in the square 5x7 matrix.

rows.name: Pixel cube
rows.rationale: R1-02 redrawn as 2:1 pixel art on the 16-cell grid, the way BAM's hammer is drawn in pixels: three shaded faces and a 2x3 copper port. Wordmark in the square 5x7 matrix.

rows.name: RP tile
rows.rationale: BAM's tile system applied straight: R and P knocked out of a dark tile with BAM's rx-4 corners; the wordmark is pixel capitals on BAM's 10-unit grid at BAM's letter size, reusing BAM's own B and A, with PARTS in BAM Green.

rows.name: RP tile
rows.rationale: BAM's tile system applied straight: R and P knocked out of a dark tile with BAM's rx-4 corners; the wordmark is pixel capitals on BAM's 10-unit grid at BAM's letter size, reusing BAM's own B and A, with PARTS in BAM Green.

rows.name: Square matrix
rows.rationale: R1-14 moved onto BAM's square pixel: the same 5x7 lowercase, solid square cells, 'parts' in copper. The mark is the wordmark's own p at two grid cells per pixel.

rows.name: Square matrix
rows.rationale: R1-14 moved onto BAM's square pixel: the same 5x7 lowercase, solid square cells, 'parts' in copper. The mark is the wordmark's own p at two grid cells per pixel.

rows.name: Parts bot
rows.rationale: Cellular-automaton growth: 13 square modules on a 5x5 lattice assemble bottom-up into a small robot, and the green eye is the last part placed. The animation below shows it assembling.

rows.name: Parts bot
rows.rationale: Cellular-automaton growth: 13 square modules on a 5x5 lattice assemble bottom-up into a small robot, and the green eye is the last part placed. The animation below shows it assembling.

rows.name: Quadtree
rows.rationale: Parts of parts: a square split into four, one quarter split again, and its last quarter split again in copper. Black boxes all the way down, read from small to big.

rows.name: Quadtree
rows.rationale: Parts of parts: a square split into four, one quarter split again, and its last quarter split again in copper. Black boxes all the way down, read from small to big.

rows.name: Port grid
rows.rationale: A part as a BAM tile with a 3x3 grid of ports cut through it; one port is lit green, the connection in use. Breadboard, peg board and parts drawer in one.

rows.name: Port grid
rows.rationale: A part as a BAM tile with a 3x3 grid of ports cut through it; one port is lit green, the connection in use. Breadboard, peg board and parts drawer in one.

rows.name: Block stack
rows.rationale: Six square blocks stacked 3-2-1, the copper part placed on top: small parts building something bigger, the stacking blocks Zach liked in BAM's round 1.

rows.name: Block stack
rows.rationale: Six square blocks stacked 3-2-1, the copper part placed on top: small parts building something bigger, the stacking blocks Zach liked in BAM's round 1.

rows.name: Joint
rows.rationale: Two parts locked together: a stepped dovetail key in green held in an ink block. robotparts is about how parts fit (interfaces, mounts, connectors).

rows.name: Joint
rows.rationale: Two parts locked together: a stepped dovetail key in green held in an ink block. robotparts is about how parts fit (interfaces, mounts, connectors).

rows.name: Stud brick
rows.rationale: R1-11 made into a building block: 'parts' knocked out of a copper brick with four studs on top, so it snaps onto 'robot'. The mark is a studded brick with a pixel p cut through it.

rows.name: Stud brick
rows.rationale: R1-11 made into a building block: 'parts' knocked out of a copper brick with four studs on top, so it snaps onto 'robot'. The mark is a studded brick with a pixel p cut through it.

rows.name: Toolbox
rows.rationale: R1-11 as a toolbox: 'parts' sits in an ink box with a green carry handle. The mark is the same box with a pixel p.

rows.name: Toolbox
rows.rationale: R1-11 as a toolbox: 'parts' sits in an ink box with a green carry handle. The mark is the same box with a pixel p.

rows.name: PARTS tile
rows.rationale: R1-11 spliced into BAM's system: ROBOT in BAM's pixel capitals, PARTS knocked out of one dark tile in BAM's proportions (5-cell letters, 2-cell margin, rx 4 of 90), with two square green studs so the tile is a brick. The mark is P in a studded tile.

rows.name: PARTS tile
rows.rationale: R1-11 spliced into BAM's system: ROBOT in BAM's pixel capitals, PARTS knocked out of one dark tile in BAM's proportions (5-cell letters, 2-cell margin, rx 4 of 90), with two square green studs so the tile is a brick. The mark is P in a studded tile.

rows.name: Pixel letters
rows.rationale: Asks whether the brick should speak BAM's pixel language, making robotparts BAM's sibling through the type as well as the grid.

rows.name: Pixel letters
rows.rationale: Asks whether the brick should speak BAM's pixel language, making robotparts BAM's sibling through the type as well as the grid.

rows.name: Two bricks
rows.rationale: Asks whether the name itself should be assembled from parts: the robot is a brick and parts is the brick that joins it. The two-block rhythm also echoes BAM's row of letter tiles.

rows.name: Two bricks
rows.rationale: Asks whether the name itself should be assembled from parts: the robot is a brick and parts is the brick that joins it. The two-block rhythm also echoes BAM's row of letter tiles.

rows.name: Ink brick, copper studs
rows.rationale: Asks whether copper should be the brick or the highlight. This is BAM's own discipline (mono plus one highlight) applied to 10: the brick reads as a black-box part and the copper studs are the connection points.

rows.name: Ink brick, copper studs
rows.rationale: Asks whether copper should be the brick or the highlight. This is BAM's own discipline (mono plus one highlight) applied to 10: the brick reads as a black-box part and the copper studs are the connection points.

rows.name: Extruded brick
rows.rationale: Asks whether the brick should be an object you could pick up (a part) rather than a flat sign.

rows.name: Extruded brick
rows.rationale: Asks whether the brick should be an object you could pick up (a part) rather than a flat sign.

rows.name: Plain brick mark
rows.rationale: Asks whether the favicon needs the letter, or whether the brick alone carries robotparts.

rows.name: Plain brick mark
rows.rationale: Asks whether the favicon needs the letter, or whether the brick alone carries robotparts.

rows.name: One stud
rows.rationale: A single wide stud centred on the brick. One stud is the unit (one part), and it steps away from the familiar two-by-something toy brick.

rows.name: One stud
rows.rationale: A single wide stud centred on the brick. One stud is the unit (one part), and it steps away from the familiar two-by-something toy brick.

rows.name: Square studs, sharp corners
rows.rationale: Narrow square studs on a sharp-cornered brick: machined rather than moulded, a part off a mill.

rows.name: Square studs, sharp corners
rows.rationale: Narrow square studs on a sharp-cornered brick: machined rather than moulded, a part off a mill.

rows.name: Three studs, squat
rows.rationale: A low 1x3 brick with three studs and no letter in the mark. In the lockup the three studs sit over the right of the brick only, so the word has room.

rows.name: Three studs, squat
rows.rationale: A low 1x3 brick with three studs and no letter in the mark. In the lockup the three studs sit over the right of the brick only, so the word has room.

rows.name: Pill brick
rows.rationale: The brick's corners rounded all the way to a pill: softer and friendlier, still studded.

rows.name: Pill brick
rows.rationale: The brick's corners rounded all the way to a pill: softer and friendlier, still studded.

rows.name: Ring studs from above
rows.rationale: A 2x2 brick seen from directly above: four hollow ring studs on a square tile, the view you see when you reach into a parts bin.

rows.name: Ring studs from above
rows.rationale: A 2x2 brick seen from directly above: four hollow ring studs on a square tile, the view you see when you reach into a parts bin.

rows.name: Half-height studs
rows.rationale: Low, wide studs, more like a plate or a machined boss than a toy: five on the lockup's brick (odd count), two on the mark.

rows.name: Half-height studs
rows.rationale: Low, wide studs, more like a plate or a machined boss than a toy: five on the lockup's brick (odd count), two on the mark.

rows.name: Studs above, sockets below
rows.rationale: Studs on top and matching sockets cut from the bottom edge: a part that connects both ways, to what is above and to what is below.

rows.name: Studs above, sockets below
rows.rationale: Studs on top and matching sockets cut from the bottom edge: a part that connects both ways, to what is above and to what is below.

rows.name: Sockets cut from the top
rows.rationale: The studs inverted into round sockets bitten out of the top edge: the brick waiting for the next part.

rows.name: Sockets cut from the top
rows.rationale: The studs inverted into round sockets bitten out of the top edge: the brick waiting for the next part.

rows.name: Outline brick
rows.rationale: The brick as a single outline, stroke weight matched to the type; the mark has no letter, just the hollow brick.

rows.name: Outline brick
rows.rationale: The brick as a single outline, stroke weight matched to the type; the mark has no letter, just the hollow brick.

rows.name: Word on an upturned plate
rows.rationale: A plate turned over under 'parts': the word stands on its flat back, and the studs hang underneath like feet.

rows.name: Word on an upturned plate
rows.rationale: A plate turned over under 'parts': the word stands on its flat back, and the studs hang underneath like feet.

rows.name: The o is a brick
rows.rationale: Both o's in 'robot' become a 1x1 brick seen from above, a ring stud on a rounded square, so the robot is literally built of parts.

rows.name: The o is a brick
rows.rationale: Both o's in 'robot' become a 1x1 brick seen from above, a ring stud on a rounded square, so the robot is literally built of parts.

rows.name: Studs on the letters
rows.rationale: No brick at all: studs grow out of the tops of p, a, r and s (placed on measured glyph positions), and the mark is a p carrying two studs.

rows.name: Studs on the letters
rows.rationale: No brick at all: studs grow out of the tops of p, a, r and s (placed on measured glyph positions), and the mark is a p carrying two studs.

rows.name: Brick robot head
rows.rationale: The brick is a robot's head: its two studs become ears and two round eyes and a mouth are cut through it.

rows.name: Brick robot head
rows.rationale: The brick is a robot's head: its two studs become ears and two round eyes and a mouth are cut through it.

rows.name: Peg over socket
rows.rationale: Two slabs about to join: a peg on the upper part hangs over the matching socket in the lower one, one gap apart.

rows.name: Peg over socket
rows.rationale: Two slabs about to join: a peg on the upper part hangs over the matching socket in the lower one, one gap apart.

rows.name: Isometric, one ink
rows.rationale: A 1x1 brick in isometric, drawn as one ink with its edges as cut lines: round 1's 02 cube, now a brick, with no shading tone.

rows.name: Isometric, one ink
rows.rationale: A 1x1 brick in isometric, drawn as one ink with its edges as cut lines: round 1's 02 cube, now a brick, with no shading tone.

rows.name: Offset stack
rows.rationale: Three bricks stacked and offset like a wall, the top one studded: parts building up.

rows.name: Offset stack
rows.rationale: Three bricks stacked and offset like a wall, the top one studded: parts building up.

rows.name: Long brick under the whole word
rows.rationale: The whole name knocked out of one long eight-stud brick; the mark is the same idea shrunk to a slim plate with four studs.

rows.name: Long brick under the whole word
rows.rationale: The whole name knocked out of one long eight-stud brick; the mark is the same idea shrunk to a slim plate with four studs.

rows.name: A 1x1 brick as the full stop
rows.rationale: robotparts has no i to dot, so the smallest part becomes the full stop: a 1x1 brick after the word. The mark is that one brick.

rows.name: A 1x1 brick as the full stop
rows.rationale: robotparts has no i to dot, so the smallest part becomes the full stop: a 1x1 brick after the word. The mark is that one brick.

rows.name: Brick on its end
rows.rationale: The brick stood on its end so the studs point forward, toward the next part, with the p reading upright in the face.

rows.name: Brick on its end
rows.rationale: The brick stood on its end so the studs point forward, toward the next part, with the p reading upright in the face.

rows.name: parts hangs from a plate
rows.rationale: A studded plate with 'parts' hanging from its underside, like a part on a rail; the mark is a p hanging from a plate.

rows.name: parts hangs from a plate
rows.rationale: A studded plate with 'parts' hanging from its underside, like a part on a rail; the mark is a p hanging from a plate.

rows.name: Stud brick, in black and white
rows.rationale: Round 2's 10 with its copper swapped for ink and nothing else changed: 'robot' plain, 'parts' knocked out of a brick with four round studs; the mark is a two-stud brick with a pixel p.

rows.name: Stud brick, in black and white
rows.rationale: Round 2's 10 with its copper swapped for ink and nothing else changed: 'robot' plain, 'parts' knocked out of a brick with four round studs; the mark is a two-stud brick with a pixel p.

rows.name: The lockup's p
rows.rationale: The p from 'parts', exactly: Liberation Sans Bold, widened 1.144x as the lockup widens it, knocked out of R2-10's brick at the size that fills the body with clear space on every side.

rows.name: Heavier p
rows.rationale: The same p grown by a round-joined stroke (Liberation Sans stops at Bold), so the stem and bowl hold more pixels at 16 px.

rows.name: rp
rows.rationale: 'rp' in the lockup's bold, lower case, at the font's own spacing: robot and parts both present in the icon.

rows.name: rp, joined
rows.rationale: r and p pulled together until r's arm runs into p's stem, one connected shape: two parts joined.

rows.name: RP capitals
rows.rationale: R and P capitals in the lockup's bold: the formal, monogram reading.

rows.name: One stud
rows.rationale: The lockup's p on a one-stud brick: round 4's best silhouette with the real letter.

rows.name: p placed low
rows.rationale: The p dropped until its descender runs out through the bottom edge, leaving a solid band of ink under the studs so they read as studs, not as bumps on the letter.

rows.name: Lockup radius
rows.rationale: 01 with the brick's corner and stud radii set to the lockup brick's in proportion (rx 3 on a 36-tall brick, so rx 4 on the mark's 48-tall body).

rows.name: Outlined p
rows.rationale: The lockup's p as an outline cut into the brick, not a solid knockout: lighter, more technical.

rows.name: Four studs
rows.rationale: The mark borrows the lockup brick's four studs, so the icon is a square crop of the 'parts' brick with its p.

rows.name: Today's mark: pixel P
rows.rationale: R2-10's mark as it stands: the two-stud brick with a pixel p cut through it. The brick is settled; the letter is what this round replaces, because it does not match the lockup's sans.

rows.name: r regular, p bold
rows.rationale: The direct mirror of the lockup: a thin r from 'robot' (Regular) and a bold p from 'parts' (Bold), both knocked out, spaced a touch tighter than the font's own so the pair reads as one unit.

rows.name: r outside the brick
rows.rationale: An ink r on the background beside a smaller brick with the bold p knocked out of it: 'robot' beside the 'parts' brick, shrunk to a square. The brick is 11 by 8 grid cells so its edges still land on whole pixels.

rows.name: r tucked into p
rows.rationale: The regular r pulled in until its arm reaches over to p's stem: robot and parts joined into one glyph, thin into bold.

rows.name: p larger
rows.rationale: The bold p set larger than the regular r, its descender running out through the brick's bottom edge (round 5's 07): parts is the hero, robot the qualifier.

rows.name: Both bold, heavier (control)
rows.rationale: 03 as picked (both bold), grown by round 5's 02 stroke and spaced open so the heavier letters do not touch: the legibility ceiling to judge the others against.

rows.name: rp, both bold (as picked)
rows.rationale: Round 5's 03 unchanged: r and p both in the lockup's bold, knocked out of R2-10's brick.

rows.name: Outline brick
rows.rationale: The live brick drawn as one 3.5-unit outline (1.5 px in the 28 px header) with its four studs as bumps in the outline; 'parts' sits inside in bold ink.

rows.name: Outline brick round the whole name
rows.rationale: One outline brick with six studs around the whole word 'robotparts': the name is the part, and nothing sits beside a block.

rows.name: Studs only
rows.rationale: No body: just the brick's studded top edge, a thin cap with four studs, sitting over the bold 'parts'.

rows.name: Studded plate under the word
rows.rationale: 'robotparts' stands on a thin studded plate, like letters built on a baseplate; the p's descender drops into a socket cut through the plate.

rows.name: Outline brick, solid studs
rows.rationale: 01's outline brick with its four studs left solid: the body is open, so there is no filled tag, and the solid studs keep the brick's weight at small sizes.

rows.name: Live: reads like a filled tag
rows.rationale: The lockup on the site today: 'robot' plain beside a solid four-stud brick with 'parts' knocked out of it.

rows.name: Live: reads like a filled tag
rows.rationale: The lockup on the site today: 'robot' plain beside a solid four-stud brick with 'parts' knocked out of it.

rows.name: Dimetric brick, shaded in one ink
rows.rationale: The brick turned a little: a long front face sloping 10 degrees carries the knocked-out 'parts', a hatched end face climbs away on the right, and the open top face holds four studs as solid cylinders with open tops.

rows.name: Front brick with a top plane
rows.rationale: The live front face, seen a little from above: a thin open top plane appears behind the studs, and the studs become short cylinders with open elliptical tops and a knocked-out highlight line.

rows.name: Extruded, one ink
rows.rationale: The live brick unchanged, with a solid side and bottom extruded down-right in the same ink, separated from the front face by a thin paper gap (round 3's D was two colours; this is one).

rows.name: Line-art dimetric
rows.rationale: 01's dimetric brick as line art: every face and stud an outline, 'parts' in bold ink on the front face. Ties to round 7's outline brick.

rows.name: Tilted brick, snapping down
rows.rationale: 02's brick (top plane, cylinder studs) tilted 6 degrees, as if it is being snapped down onto the line 'robot' sits on: depth plus motion.

rows.name: Live: reads like a filled tag
rows.rationale: The lockup on the site today: 'robot' plain beside a solid four-stud brick with 'parts' knocked out of it.

rows.name: Live: reads like a filled tag
rows.rationale: The lockup on the site today: 'robot' plain beside a solid four-stud brick with 'parts' knocked out of it.

rows.name: Two bricks side by side
rows.rationale: The simplest answer to 'both in cubes': two equal bricks in one view, a small gap between them.

rows.name: Snapped end to end
rows.rationale: The two bricks pressed together into one longer part, the seam a single shared edge: robot and parts literally connected.

rows.name: parts stacked on robot
rows.rationale: parts snapped on top of robot, robot's first stud left showing so the connection reads.

rows.name: robot built from parts
rows.rationale: The story in one picture: a robot built from parts, the big brick carrying robot and the small one parts.

rows.name: One long 1x8 brick
rows.rationale: For comparison: one long brick carries the whole name, eight studs.

rows.name: A step
rows.rationale: A staircase of two bricks, parts climbing off robot: movement without chaos.

rows.name: Three studs each, both bold
rows.rationale: Zach's 'cubes': three studs make each brick nearly cube-shaped, and both words go Bold so they hold their weight on the faces.

rows.name: Two angles
rows.rationale: Playful but held: robot slopes down 9 degrees, parts tips up 4, so the pair looks handled rather than printed.

rows.name: Heavy contour, light top
rows.rationale: R8-04 with an illustrator's line hierarchy: a heavier outer contour, lighter top face and studs.

rows.name: Filled studs, outline body
rows.rationale: R8-04 with the favicon's solid studs on the outline body, so lockup and favicon share their studs.

rows.name: Line-art dimetric (round 8's 04)
rows.rationale: The direction Zach picked: an outline dimetric brick with cylinder studs, 'parts' on its front face, plain 'robot' beside it.

rows.name: Shallow, 3 deep
rows.rationale: R8-03 with the extrusion cut to 3 units (gap 1.2, so a side still shows).

rows.name: Deep, 8
rows.rationale: R8-03 swept 8 units: the brick becomes a slab. Shown with the favicon extruded the same way (rounded sweep).

rows.name: Down-left
rows.rationale: The extrusion runs down-left, toward 'robot'; the brick moves right 8 so they clear.

rows.name: Straight down, body only
rows.rationale: The extrusion drops straight down from the body alone; the studs stay flat.

rows.name: No gap, hatched
rows.rationale: No paper gap, so the hatching alone separates the side from the face.

rows.name: Real side face
rows.rationale: A true oblique projection: the body's right and bottom faces and each stud's right face as sharp polygons. Shown with the favicon extruded the same way.

rows.name: Drop shadow (period look)

rows.name: Double step
